title: Invert the delegation default: main works, delegation is the exception
context: rules/common/delegation-discipline.md mandated delegating every code mutation, "including a one-line typo fix, at a known ~5-10k-token round-trip cost, accepted by design". Measurement of the incident put the floor at 137,191 tokens for the cheapest real dispatch and a median of 399,976 — 14 to 27 times the declared figure at the floor. Because delegation was mandatory, dispatching was the rule-following action and doing the work inline was a violation, so the router was biased toward the expensive option by design.
options: Keep the mandate and correct the declared cost figure
Add a routing agent or routing skill that decides when to delegate
Invert the default so the main thread works and delegation is the exception needing a named reason
outcome: Inverted. delegation-discipline.md is deleted and replaced with four named reasons to delegate, which map one-to-one onto the five retained agents so the roster itself is the structural half of the pairing. A routing mistake now fails toward "main did it itself", which is cheap and usually correct. This makes routing accuracy non-load-bearing rather than attempting to make routing accurate — a routing agent was rejected because it adds a new advisory layer for a decision that cannot be made deterministic.
